analysis.title: DeskTalk - US Midterms: Into the final week
key_insights: US midterms are one week away. The consensus view is that knee-jerk market moves will be avoided in the immediate aftermath, and a crowded macro calendar this week (FOMC, other central bank decisions, earnings, fiscal risks) has largely overshadowed the election as an event risk.

A Democratic House is largely expected, so the margin of victory matters. Cook Political Report lists just 17 toss-up House races (~4% of all House seats), so the bar for Democrats to retake the House is low.
Nate Silver sees a 75% chance of a Democratic Senate win, which is more bullish than prediction markets. He also notes that individual Senate battleground polling is extremely tight.
Citi's bottom line: prediction markets suggest a Democratic sweep is increasingly priced, but Citi continues to view the Senate as a genuine toss-up.

Positioning reflects other macro risks more than the election. Investors are adding bearish positions to US equities, USD remains net long with risk of outflows after last week's leveraged selling, and Treasuries have flipped tactically long into FOMC. Refunding takes more focus on Nov 4.

Citi Global Macro Strategy finds that day-one price action after midterm elections shows negative follow-through over the following days. A pullback after a Democratic sweep would offer a buy-the-dip opportunity, especially for SPX and DXY.
Treasuries are an exception: t+1 price action is generally positive or flat after midterms, and the curve flattens.
Early voting is above 32m votes. Registered Democrats account for 45% of early votes in states that report party registration, versus 39% for Republicans.
Most states can pre-process mail ballots, which should support timely results on election night. Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New Hampshire may take longer to report if races are tight.

Early results from North Carolina, Kansas and especially Texas could give clues on election night. A Democratic win in Texas would likely accelerate pricing of a broader Democratic sweep during the Tokyo session.
